Subject: MAP: cost/QoS sanity check request

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the prefix caching idea. Before we finalize the MAP and internal procurement timeline, Finance and Platform want a quick sanity check on unit economics: tokens per interaction, expected tokens/$ under our traffic, and whether caching/batching assumptions hold for our distribution.

I've attached a small traffic sample (Atlas_traffic_profile_sample.csv) and our expected concurrency ranges (p95 peaks ~320 qps). Can Redwood run a short simulation using the recommended model variants (redwood-5 base and a 4-bit quant variant) and show:
- tokens/request (mean / p95) under our prompt/response lengths
- effective tokens/$ estimates under 3 batching strategies (no batching, batch=8, batch=16)
- sensitivity to prefix/KV cache hit rates (20% / 50% / 80%)

Our procurement deadline is end of week — can you turn this around by Thu 9/17? If not, what’s the earliest?

Best,
Samir Patel
VP Product, Atlas Health

Samir — thanks for the sample and the clear ask. We can handle this and will deliver a short simulation + updated MAP cost sheet. Proposed plan:

1) Quick triage (today / tomorrow): Karthik will validate the traffic sample and baseline prompt/response length assumptions.
2) Run sims (Karthik): token-level simulation for redwood-5 and a 4-bit quant variant across the three batching scenarios you mentioned. We’ll model KV/prefix cache hit rates at 20/50/80% and include aggregate tokens/$ and per-request latency distributions.
3) Deliverable (Thu 9/17 EOD PDT):
   - MAP-cost-checklist-v1.xlsx (assumptions + tokens per scenario)
   - token_simulation_results.csv (per-scenario CSV)
   - short one-page summary with recommendation (batching vs cache priority)

A few quick clarifying asks so we set the sim correctly:
- Are the response length distributions in column "resp_tokens" of the CSV representative of full responses (with few follow-ups)?
- Do you have a hard p95 latency SLO we should respect when choosing batching windows (e.g., 300ms p95 for critical flows vs 1s for non-critical)?

I’ve attached a checklist (MAP-cost-checklist-v1.xlsx) that we’ll fill during the run. If that timeline works I’ll mark the MAP milestone in HubSpot and route the results to your procurement lead.

Thanks — kim

Kim / Samir — I reviewed the sample and ran a small local pass to sanity-check token counts. Quick notes and the parameters I’ll use for the formal sim:

Assumptions I infer from the CSV:
- mean prompt tokens: ~120 (std 40)
- mean response tokens: ~340 (std 120)
- median conversation length: 1.1 turns (most interactions are single-turn)

Planned sim parameters (will commit code + CSV outputs):
- Models: redwood-5 (fp16) and redwood-5-4bit (q4_0 equivalent profile)
- Batching windows: none (per-request), batch=8 (up to 150ms window), batch=16 (up to 300ms window) — these windows chosen to keep p95 latency reasonable for customer-critical flows.
- Cache model: prefix/KV hit-rate sweep [0.2, 0.5, 0.8] — treat hits as zero prompt tokens for prefixes and only response/continuation tokens billed.
- Cost inputs: use current hosted pricebook (internal) and our quantization multiplier (4-bit = ~0.38x token compute cost).
- Output metrics: tokens/request (mean/p95), tokens per 1M requests, effective tokens/$, latency p50/p95 per scheduling config, and a delta table showing cost savings from caching vs batching.

One more thing — can you confirm if Atlas wants prefetch/KV pinning for specific prefixes? That changes cache hit modeling (we can model sticky prefixes vs ephemeral).

I’ll push the sim results and token_simulation_results.csv by Thu 9/17 14:00 PDT. If we can get a hard latency SLO, I’ll include the ops-safe config (batch size / window) that keeps p95 under that threshold.

— Karthik
Lead ML Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
